jawa-1-lng-power-fishers.conditions_add: ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement (2009) applied to the loan. The project was classified Category A for environment, B for involuntary resettlement and C for Indigenous Peoples, a resettlement plan was prepared setting out entitlements and a livelihood restoration strategy, and semi-annual safeguard and social monitoring reports are published on ADB's website during implementation (ADB Compliance Review Panel, 2025). ADB's 2018 announcement of the financing says it included targets for women's employment and training "to be monitored by ADB".

why.safeguard: ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement (2009) applied to the loan

jawa-1-lng-power-fishers.searched: Opened the ADB CRP eligibility report and the ADB news release on the financing; the JBIC press release gives only the loan amount and says repayment comes solely from project cash flows, with no conditions stated.

phnom-penh-hcmc-highway-nr1.conditions_add: ADB's evaluation of the project says the Cambodian part carried 12 standard loan covenants, including covenants on resettlement and compensation, on environmental mitigation, on road maintenance and on holding tripartite coordination meetings with Viet Nam and ADB two or three times a year. The government and the Ministry of Public Works and Transport "fully complied with 7 (58%) of 12 standard loan covenants", with partial compliance on resettlement and compensation, environmental mitigation and maintenance. The government was also to finance US$10.7 million of the local currency cost and provided US$7.1 million (ADB Operations Evaluation Department, 2008).

why.safeguard: covenants on resettlement and compensation, on environmental mitigation, on road maintenance

phnom-penh-hcmc-highway-nr1.searched: Opened the ADB Special Project Facilitator final report (no covenant text) and the ADB Operations Evaluation performance evaluation via OECD DEReC, which lists covenant compliance.

sendou-bargny-coal.conditions_add: The African Development Bank's Independent Review Mechanism found that "key policy covenants were not included in the Credit of Agreement on environmental and social measures", and that no Resettlement Action Plan containing compensation measures and livelihood support was prepared before approval; the bank's 2003 involuntary resettlement policy, 2004 environment policy and 2000 environmental review procedures for private sector operations applied, and the remedial measures later required a marine impact assessment, an ash management plan and a water supply impact study (AfDB IRM third monitoring report, 2022). FMO's complaints mechanism assessed the plant against the IFC Performance Standards and found non-compliance with Performance Standards 1, 3 and 5 (ICM, 2023).

why.safeguard: assessed the plant against the IFC Performance Standards and found non-compliance with Performance Standards 1, 3 and 5

sendou-bargny-coal.searched: Opened the AfDB IRM third monitoring report and the FMO ICM second monitoring report; neither reproduces the loan agreements, and the IRM states the environmental and social covenants were left out of the credit agreement.

nyamagasani-hydro.conditions_add: FMO says Frontier Energy has followed "the Environmental and Social Action Plan developed by FMO for the project", and that FMO monitored resettlement, displacement and compensation with its independent environmental and social adviser and reviewed the grievance register. The complaints were reviewed against IFC Performance Standards 1, 4 and 5 (ICM preliminary review, 2021). The reports opened do not set out the terms of the US$39 million facility agreement.

why.safeguard: the Environmental and Social Action Plan developed by FMO for the project

nyamagasani-hydro.searched: Opened the FMO ICM preliminary review report for complaints 20-001 and 20-003; it names the ESAP and the Performance Standards but gives no conditions precedent or disbursement conditions.

thilawa-sez-resettlement.conditions_add: JICA's Guidelines for Environmental and Social Considerations applied to the project. Under them affected people must be consulted, compensation should as far as possible be paid in advance at full replacement cost, and for large-scale resettlement a plan must be prepared and made public; the Resettlement Work Plan was finalised on 22 November 2013 after a public comment period, and JICA's experts monitored its preparation (JICA examiners, 2014). The examiners describe JICA's input on compensation amounts and its June 2014 proposal to dig deeper wells as advice and proposals, not conditions of its funding.

why.safeguard: JICA's Guidelines for Environmental and Social Considerations applied to the project

thilawa-sez-resettlement.searched: Opened the JICA Examiner investigation report on the Thilawa Class A Area; it contains no loan or investment agreement conditions.

nagdhunga-tunnel-water.conditions_add: The project was classified Category B under JICA's Guidelines for Environmental and Social Considerations in January 2014 and was not reclassified. Minutes of Discussions agreed between JICA and the Government of Nepal on 13 November 2014 included an agreement that "water regime and water use" would be monitored; the monitoring reports did not cover that item until the third quarter of 2021 (JICA examiners, 2026). The report does not set out the terms of the 16,636 million yen loan agreement.

why.safeguard: an agreement that "water regime and water use" would be monitored

nagdhunga-tunnel-water.searched: Opened the JICA Examiners' investigation report on the Nagdhunga Tunnel; it has no loan terms and no procurement conditions.

buchanan-renewables-liberia.conditions_add: Both loans were governed by OPIC's Environmental Handbook of February 2004, and for the 2011 expansion loan the company agreed to comply with the relevant IFC Performance Standards, which OPIC then wrote into contract conditions that made them enforceable. At the December 2008 commitment OPIC required the company to report baseline environmental conditions for properties expected to be harvested in the following six months, a Harvest Operations Plan for each site covering drainage, buffer zones and cultural features, and annual Harvest Management Plans with site-specific environmental baseline data (OPIC Office of Accountability, 2014).

why.safeguard: OPIC required the company to report baseline environmental conditions ... a Harvest Operations Plan for each site

buchanan-renewables-liberia.searched: Opened the OPIC Office of Accountability review of the Buchanan Renewables projects, which sets out the Environmental Handbook, the IFC Performance Standards written into the expansion loan contract, and the harvest plan requirements.

san-bartolome-potosi.conditions_add: OPIC's environmental clearance required eight environment-related plans to be submitted by April 2005, and the December 2004 contract of insurance incorporated all of them except the resettlement plan. The clearance had said the contract "should require Manquiri to prepare a Resettlement Action Plan"; that requirement was dropped with no documented reason, and the contract contains no reference to any Indigenous Peoples planning process. OPIC asked about a resettlement action plan after a site visit in June 2007 and was given a 15-page compensation summary (OPIC Office of Accountability, 2009).

why.safeguard: the December 2004 contract of insurance incorporated all of them except the resettlement plan

san-bartolome-potosi.searched: Opened the OPIC Office of Accountability compliance review of the San Bartolome project, which compares the environmental clearance requirements with the insurance contract.

mozambique-lng-afungi.conditions_add: US EXIM said it "will require the implementation of environmental and social management plans in the project's financial documents", that it "required that the Mozambique LNG project submit an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA)" for review, and that the project must maintain a transparent and effective grievance mechanism; it also said the contract's US content requirement would continue to apply, with the EXIM-supported goods and services provided from the United States (EXIM, 2019). For the neighbouring Rovuma project, DFC's board approval of up to US$1.5 billion of political risk insurance was contingent on DFC reinsuring at least US$1 billion, and DFC's 2017 policy states that projects must meet the IFC Performance Standards; DFC never signed an insurance contract (DFC Independent Accountability Mechanism, 2025).

why.safeguard: will require the implementation of environmental and social management plans in the project's financial documents
why.tied: the contract's US content requirement would continue to apply, with the EXIM-supported goods and services provided from the United States

mozambique-lng-afungi.searched: Opened the EXIM press release on the US$5 billion authorisation and the DFC IAM appraisal report on Rovuma LNG; no UKEF or AfDB condition documents were opened.

san-roque-dam-agno.conditions_add: Friends of the Earth Japan says JBIC set four preconditions on the US$400 million loan to the National Power Corporation in 1999: confirm the number of people to be relocated from the reservoir area and obtain their consent; consult and survey affected people other than relocatees, including Indigenous peoples; secure remedies for all affected people, with consideration for Indigenous peoples; and "to establish monitoring system for the environmental and social issues". It says the preconditions were not met and the financing was fully disbursed by January 2005 (FoE Japan, via Housing and Land Rights Network, 2006).

why.safeguard: JBIC set four preconditions on the US$400 million loan to the National Power Corporation in 1999

san-roque-dam-agno.searched: Opened the FoE Japan case paper hosted by the Housing and Land Rights Network, which lists the four JBIC preconditions; JBIC's own loan documents for the 1998 SRPC loan were not found online.

kotopanjang-dam.conditions_add: JICA's ex-post evaluation says Japan's ODA loan was extended under "the Indonesian commitment to pay sufficient attention to social and environmental impacts", and that the environmental management plan (RKL) and environmental monitoring plan (RPL) were approved in 1989. The evaluation frames this as a commitment rather than a covenant and does not set out the terms of loan agreements IP-358 and IP-374 (JICA ex-post evaluation, 2004).
kotopanjang-dam.searched: Opened the JICA third-party ex-post evaluation of the Kotapanjang project; it has no loan terms table, no procurement classification and no stated covenants.

ramu-nickel-basamuk.conditions_add: AidData's record of the US$560 million China Eximbank facility, committed on 23 July 2008, lists a 10-year maturity, a US dollar portion at LIBOR (3.119 percent at the time) plus a 1.6 percent margin and a renminbi portion at about 4.7 percent, with repayment by 2017, eight years after the mine started. The record lists no collateral, guarantee or policy conditions, and states no requirement to use a Chinese contractor, although China Metallurgical Group was the EPC contractor (AidData, record 64520).
ramu-nickel-basamuk.searched: Opened AidData record 64520 for the Ramu loan; it gives pricing and maturity but records no conditions, collateral or tied procurement.

bisha-mine-forced-labour.searched: Opened AidData record 56386, which describes a variable-rate commercial loan of US$80 million to the Government of Eritrea in November 2007 and records no collateral, guarantee, repayment source, maturity, tied procurement or conditions; no China Eximbank loan document for Bisha was found.

tagaung-taung-nickel.searched: Opened AidData record 34115: interest type is "Unknown", the amounts of the CDB and China Eximbank loans are not public, and no collateral, guarantee, repayment source or loan conditions are recorded; the US$300,000 a year community spending it mentions comes from the mining contract with CNMC, not the loan.

techo-airport-land.searched: Opened AidData record 61125, which says "the borrowing terms of the loan are unknown" and records no interest rate, maturity, collateral, guarantee, repayment source or tied procurement; the land disputes it describes are not recorded as loan conditions.

hambantota-port-zone-clashes.conditions_add: AidData's record of the US$306.7 million buyer's credit says China Eximbank lent to the Government of Sri Lanka, which passed the money on to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority. The terms were six-month LIBOR plus a 0.9 percent margin, changed to a fixed 6.3 percent in an October 2008 restructuring, a 15-year maturity with a four-year grace period, a 0.3 percent management fee, a 0.3 percent commitment fee and a 6 percent Sinosure insurance premium payable in two equal instalments within two years of signing, with a 1 percent penalty rate on overdue amounts. Under the 2017 port concession, responsibility for repaying the loan moved from the Ports Authority to the General Treasury. The record states no collateral, no sovereign guarantee and no formal tied-procurement condition (AidData, record 33256).

why.repay: China Eximbank lent to the Government of Sri Lanka, which passed the money on to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority

hambantota-port-zone-clashes.searched: Opened AidData record 33256 for the Phase I buyer's credit; its pricing, maturity, grace period, fees and repayment arrangements are set out there.

peshawar-brt-traders-underpasses.conditions_add: ADB classified the project Category A for environment and Category A for involuntary resettlement. Its project page says the government must ensure the design "minimizes land acquisition and resettlement impacts", that the works comply with "the approved resettlement plan and livelihood restoration plan", that the environmental impact assessment and environmental management plan are followed, and that the draft and approved final land acquisition and resettlement plan are uploaded to the agency's and ADB's websites. Retroactive financing was capped at US$97 million and bid invitations under advance contracting needed ADB approval (ADB project page, loan 3543).

why.safeguard: the works comply with "the approved resettlement plan and livelihood restoration plan"

peshawar-brt-traders-underpasses.searched: Opened the ADB project page for 48289-002, which lists the safeguard categories and the safeguard requirements; covenant texts are not published there.

balakot-hydropower-demolitions.conditions_add: ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement (2009) applied. The project is Category A for environment and involuntary resettlement, so a Land Acquisition and Resettlement Plan and an environmental impact assessment were prepared during processing and two further final plans during implementation. The plan required prior notice to every affected household, "sufficient time (6 months) after the payment of compensation and allowance" before people vacate, an independent valuation by a third-party expert, hiring of residents of Mouza Bela Sacha with training and access to credit, and an income and livelihood programme; the ADB project team said "there should be no physical displacement unless the affected people are fully paid" (ADB Compliance Review Panel, 2024).

why.safeguard: a Land Acquisition and Resettlement Plan and an environmental impact assessment were prepared during processing

balakot-hydropower-demolitions.searched: Opened the ADB CRP eligibility report for Balakot; it sets out the SPS categories and the LARP requirements but not the loan covenants.

lapsiphedi-substation-tamang.conditions_add: ADB's 2009 Safeguard Policy Statement applied. The 2017 transmission project is Category A for involuntary resettlement and the 2011 project Category B, and resettlement plans were prepared for both, requiring "compensation payment prior to physical or economic displacement". The initial environmental examination said the environmental management plan "was required to be part of the bidding documents and contracts for works", and the Nepal Electricity Authority says "the acquired land is legally transferred to the NEA before civil works can commence" (ADB Compliance Review Panel, 2025).

why.safeguard: resettlement plans were prepared for both, requiring "compensation payment prior to physical or economic displacement"

lapsiphedi-substation-tamang.searched: Opened the ADB CRP eligibility report for the Nepal electricity transmission projects; the loan covenant texts are not reproduced in it.

corridor-vc-mostar-south-malo-polje.conditions_add: The EBRD financing is "a sovereign-guaranteed loan of up to EUR 180 million" to the Motorways of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in two tranches of up to EUR 120 million and up to EUR 60 million, with the bank's risk rating for the project recorded as A (EBRD project record, via the Early Warning System). EBRD's own compliance review report and project page could not be opened, so the content of any environmental and social action plan attached to the loan was not confirmed.

why.repay: a sovereign-guaranteed loan of up to EUR 180 million

corridor-vc-mostar-south-malo-polje.searched: ebrd.com blocks automated access (robots), so the IPAM compliance review PDF and the EBRD project summary could not be opened; used the Early Warning System mirror of the EBRD project record.

ruta-del-cacao-santander.conditions_add: IDB Invest rated the road Category A and says its due diligence assesses the project "with respect to the client requirements in IDB Invest Environmental and Social Sustainability Policy", with any gaps found at that time "addressed in the Environmental and Social Action Plan". The client environmental and social documents listed for the project include an environmental management plan, a risk management plan, a biodiversity compensation plan, an abandonment plan and a chapter on resettlement (IDB Invest project page).

why.safeguard: any gaps found at that time "addressed in the Environmental and Social Action Plan"

sources_add.title: Ruta del Cacao 4G Toll Road (project page)

ruta-del-cacao-santander.searched: The MICI compliance review PDF on iadb.org redirects to a signed URL too long to fetch, so the IDB Invest project page was used for the policy and ESAP requirements.

el-dorado-fontibon-noise.searched: The MICI compliance review documents on iadb.org returned errors and could not be opened; the IDB project page for CO-L1029 lists environmental and social plans and strategy documents but states no borrower requirements, and two further PDFs found by search turned out to be other IDB cases (Pando-Monte Lirio, La Paz drainage).

costa-rica-cantonal-roads-buenos-aires.conditions_add: The IDB financing is a sovereign-guaranteed loan, operation 4507/OC-CR, with a total programme cost of US$152.04 million, of which Costa Rica had to provide US$8 million in counterpart financing. The programme is Category B, "likely to cause mostly local and short-term negative environmental and associated social impacts" with "effective mitigation measures ... readily available" (IDB project page, CR-L1065). The page lists an environmental and social management framework and management plans, dated December 2017, but does not set out the loan contract's conditions.
costa-rica-cantonal-roads-buenos-aires.searched: Opened the IDB project page for CR-L1065; the MICI eligibility memorandum on iadb.org could not be fetched, and the loan contract text is not published on the page.

wadelai-irrigation-paten.conditions_add: The African Development Bank's appraisal report sets conditions for the first disbursement: the borrower had to show it had opened a foreign currency special account at the Bank of Uganda, give a letter of comfort that the project land is "free of encumbrances" and belongs to the communities and/or government that consented to the activities, and give a letter confirming that the multisectoral steering committee "is in existence" and would stay operational. Within six months of first disbursement the government had to recruit an environmental and social development officer, a monitoring and evaluation officer, a procurement officer and an agri-business officer. The project was Environment Category 2, with an environmental and social management plan budgeted at US$850,000; the appraisal says it was anticipated that project activities would not lead to land acquisition, and it sets no resettlement plan condition (AfDB appraisal report).

why.safeguard: an environmental and social management plan budgeted at US$850,000
why.land: a letter of comfort that the project land is "free of encumbrances" and belongs to the communities and/or government that consented

sources_add.title: Uganda: Farm Income Enhancement and Forestry Conservation Programme - Project 2, appraisal report
sources_add.publisher: African Development Bank (via Early Warning System)

wadelai-irrigation-paten.searched: Opened the AfDB FIEFOC-2 appraisal report hosted by the Early Warning System, sections 3.2 and 5.2-5.3, for the safeguard category and the disbursement conditions.

leaf-ii-lakes-edward-albert.searched: Opened the Accountability Counsel/Accountability Console summary of the AfDB Independent Review Mechanism report on LEAF II; it gives the IRM's findings that the bank failed to disclose environmental and social documents and failed to enforce its own protections, and AfDB management's statement that compensation was "the borrower's responsibility", but no loan or grant agreement conditions; no AfDB appraisal report for LEAF II was located.
